scope: Actual Original cached-user SET/DEL/key ACL and plain-command success without Lua; Source only
facts: Denied SET on the cached client raises redis.exceptions.NoPermissionError before file open/build/finally; no index/file lock is created. A directory path does not contribute IsADirectoryError to the traceback because acquire failed first.
Denied plainDEL after normalWritten raises NoPermissionError, leaves committed index and locked key. Message contains actual ACL username and denied del command.
Denied key access raises NoPermissionError with argument No permissions to access a key, no index/lock. It is not an authentication failure or an invented errno.
Original index task succeeds with only connection/GET/SET/DEL/EXPIRE permissions and no EVAL: actual probe EVAL is denied while unchanged task produces SUCCESS/null, index and releasedlock.

With EVAL permitted but DEL denied, actual LuaDEL probe raises redis.exceptions.ResponseError with ACL failure in script/user_script/SHA context, unlike Original plainDEL NoPermissionError; its probevalue remains.
Safe endpoint context captures only host,port,database,authenticated username, never password/credential-bearing URL.
remaining_gates: Native owner-fenced acquire/release rawcauses and actual same-ACL differential after bounded reconnect fix.
Preserve script-vs-plain-command ACL differences; do not strip script context/invent NoPermission payload without a supported compatibilitypolicy.
No fallback to unsafe unfenced deletion, no generic AuthenticationError/ConnectionError mapping from server permissionerrors.
Only after physical settled stage/commit/release/errorcode/detail evidence may known mappings be added; timeout/ambiguity/CAS-not-owner remain operational.
